content: Proper training in insulin administration techniques is critical for individuals with diabetes and their caregivers to enhance insulin absorption and reduce the risk of complications. This training should emphasize the importance of selecting appropriate injection sites and understanding the pharmacokinetics of different types of insulin. Insulin should be injected into subcutaneous tissue rather than intramuscularly to avoid complications. Recommended injection sites include the abdomen, thighs, buttocks, and upper arms. Injecting insulin into muscle tissue can lead to unpredictable absorption due to muscle activity, which may compromise glycemic control. Rotating injection sites is essential to prevent lipohypertrophy, a condition characterized by raised, firm areas of tissue that develop from repeated injections at the same location. Lipohypertrophy can result in inconsistent insulin absorption and poor glucose management. Educational training should also focus on proper site rotation techniques and the selection of appropriate needle lengths. These measures can significantly improve the effectiveness of insulin therapy and optimize glycemic outcomes.
